subproblem.title: The Lipschitz push-forward of 3.6 is the classical push-forward for differentiable maps
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P Q n : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (V : Set (Eucl Q)) (X : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (S : GeometricCurrentOn V n) (f : Eucl P → Eucl Q), Differentiable ℝ f → IsLipschitzPushforward X f S → ∀ (ω : TestFormOn V n) (η : TestFormOn U n), (∃ N : Set (Eucl P), IsOpen N ∧ X.support ⊆ N ∧ ∀ x ∈ N, (η : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) x = ((ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl Q) n) (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x)) → S ω = X η
proof_key_steps: Unfold IsLipschitzPushforward: X = τ(M, θ, ξ), f has tangential directional derivatives L(x)v a.e., and S(ω) = ∫_M θ (L_#ξ)(ω∘f) dHⁿ.
By the sibling support-null lemma, Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. point of M lies in spt X ⊆ N.
At such points, uniqueness of the derivative of t ↦ f(x + tτ_i) gives L(x) ∘ τ = Df(x) ∘ τ on the orienting frame. Hence (L(x)_#ξ(x))(ω(f x)) = ξ(x)(Df(x)^#ω(f x)) = ξ(x)(η(x)).
The integrands of S(ω) and X(η) agree a.e. on M, so S(ω) = X(η) by integral_congr_ae.

audit.reason: The stated hypotheses match IsLipschitzPushforward exactly. Support-null supplies almost-everywhere membership in the compatibility neighbourhood. Derivative uniqueness on the orienting frame then identifies the integrands. integral_congr_ae needs no extra integrability assumption. The sole child dependency is correctly declared.
